content_voiceover: This is the study design for QUAZAR AML-001, the pivotal trial behind Onureg. It was an international, multicenter, placebo controlled, double blind phase 3 study across 148 sites in 23 countries. Key eligibility criteria at screening included patients in first complete remission or CR with incomplete count recovery after intensive chemotherapy with or without consolidation, age 55 or older, de novo or secondary AML, ECOG performance status 0 to 3, intermediate or poor risk cytogenetics, ineligibility for transplant, and adequate marrow recovery. Randomization was 1 to 1 within 4 months of achieving CR or CRi, stratified by age group, prior MDS or CMML history, cytogenetic risk, and whether consolidation was given. Patients received CC-486, that's oral azacitidine, 300 milligrams once daily for 14 days of each 28-day cycle, or matching placebo. Response was assessed every 3 cycles, patients with 5 to 15 percent marrow blasts could get an optional extended 21-day dosing schedule, and those exceeding 15 percent blasts stopped treatment. All patients were followed long-term until death, withdrawal, study termination, or loss to follow-up.
keypoints: QUAZAR AML-001: international phase 3, placebo-controlled trial of CC-486 (Onureg)
Eligibility: first CR/CRi, age 55+, intermediate/poor risk cytogenetics, transplant-ineligible
Dosing: CC-486 300 mg once daily for 14 days of each 28-day cycle vs placebo
Blast-based algorithm: extend to 21 days if 5-15% blasts, stop if over 15%
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, know the QUAZAR skeleton. This is the phase 3 trial of oral azacitidine, brand name Onureg, in older patients age 55 and up, with intermediate or poor risk AML in first remission who are not transplant candidates. The regimen is 300 milligrams daily for 14 days each 28-day cycle versus placebo, with a built-in escalation to 21 days if blasts creep up to 5 to 15 percent, and treatment stops if blasts exceed 15 percent.
